summary: This bill amends federal law to require any person transferring a firearm to provide the buyer a compatible gun lock or safety device, to stock and offer such a device for sale with every firearm, and to face civil penalties for violations.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to federal appropriations, budgets, or expenditures. It focuses exclusively on regulatory requirements for firearm transfers and storage devices.
No tax provisions, rate changes, credits, or revenue measures appear in the bill text.
The legislation does not address health insurance, medical services, public health programs, or healthcare delivery systems.

The bill directly amends 18 U.S.C. § 922(z) to expand mandatory provision of compatible gun locks to all firearm purchases (not just handguns), requires sellers to stock compatible locks, clarifies the definition of secure storage devices, and imposes civil penalties for violations. These are explicit new regulatory requirements on firearm commerce and ownership aimed at safe storage, which constitutes stricter gun regulation.
No immigration, border, visa, or asylum provisions are present.
The bill contains no language concerning reproductive rights, abortion access, or related medical regulations.
No defense appropriations, military procurement, or national security spending measures are included.
The legislation does not address environmental regulations, emissions, land use, or climate policy.
No welfare, nutrition assistance, housing, or entitlement program changes are mentioned.
The bill does not touch on schools, federal education funding, school choice, or curriculum.
No controlled substances, decriminalization, or drug enforcement provisions exist.

While the bill adds a civil penalty mechanism for violations of the new storage-device requirement, this is narrowly tied to the gun-storage mandate rather than broader sentencing reform, policing practices, or rehabilitation programs. The connection is incidental and does not meaningfully engage criminal-justice policy.
No tariffs, trade agreements, import/export rules, or globalization measures are present.
The bill does not address deficits, debt ceilings, or fiscal policy.
No provisions relate to LGBTQ+ legal protections or anti-discrimination rules.
The legislation contains no foreign-assistance authorizations or appropriations.
No election administration, voting access, or campaign-finance provisions appear.
The bill does not regulate technology companies, data collection, or privacy standards.
No labor, union, or workplace-protection measures are included.
The legislation does not address religious exemptions, civil-rights enforcement, or conflicts between religious liberty and anti-discrimination laws.
